title: Sonam Wangchuk Alleges House Arrest In Ladakh Ahead Of Peaceful Protest

ai.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk claims he is under house arrest in Ladakh with 25 personnel stationed outside his home, as he prepares for a sit-in protest demanding the release of an inquiry report and rescheduling of December council elections.

facts.claim: Wangchuk alleges house arrest, with 25 personnel posted outside home
facts.quote: - Wangchuk alleges house arrest, with 25 personnel posted outside home.

facts.claim: Authorities cite election prohibitory orders; Wangchuk will contest them legally
facts.quote: - Authorities cite election prohibitory orders; Wangchuk will contest them legally.

facts.claim: Wangchuk says security personnel, vehicles and tents have been outside his residence since Wednesday night
facts.quote: Wangchuk said security personnel, vehicles and tents have been outside his residence since Wednesday night

facts.claim: Wangchuk rejected authorities' reported position that he had merely been 'advised to stay at home'
facts.quote: Wangchuk, a prominent member of the Leh Apex Body, rejected the authorities' reported position that he had merely been "advised to stay at home".

facts.claim: Ladakh Police defended the action saying the preventive measures followed prohibitory orders from the Union Territory's Chief Electoral Officer and the Leh District Magistrate
facts.quote: Ladakh Police defended the action saying the preventive measures followed prohibitory orders from the Union Territory's Chief Electoral Officer and the Leh District Magistrate.

facts.claim: Wangchuk said the restrictions came as he and other activists were preparing a sit-in
facts.quote: Wangchuk said the restrictions came as he and other activists, including leaders of the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance, were preparing a sit-in.

facts.claim: Their demands include a rethink on the Autonomous Hill Development Council elections, scheduled for December 4
facts.quote: Their demands include a rethink on the Autonomous Hill Development Council elections, scheduled for December 4.

facts.claim: Wangchuk called a winter poll 'unacceptable', since a large part of Ladakh's population is away from the region in those months
facts.quote: Wangchuk called a winter poll "unacceptable", since a large part of Ladakh's population is away from the region in those months.

facts.claim: Wangchuk repeated his demand that the Commission of Inquiry report on the September 24 incident last year be made public
facts.quote: Wangchuk repeated his demand that the Commission of Inquiry report on the September 24 incident last year be made public, alleging that the matter is being suppressed.

ai.background_note: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk claims house arrest in Ladakh ahead of peaceful protest demanding release of inquiry report and rescheduling of December council elections.
